newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Alcatel swings back to profit, market cheers.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Alcatel swings back to profit, market cheers.

text.p: France's biggest industrial group, Alcatel Alsthom SA, on Tuesday reported a small profit for 1996 after an historic loss in 1995, prompting loud applause from investors who sent the shares surging more than five percent.
Chairman Serge Tchuruk, hired in 1995 to kick the ailing conglomerate into shape, told a news conference that Alcatel should make satisfactory profits in 1998.
It has plans to create a major defence group with allies if it wins a bidding war for state-controlled defence electronics group Thomson-CSF against Lagardere Groupe.
And the company is also talking to Britain's GEC Plc about extending cooperation beyond their GEC Alsthom transport and power generation joint venture, he said.

Alcatel turned in net attributable profit of 2.7 billion francs ($473.3 million) for 1996, slightly ahead of its own January forecast and compared with a loss of 25.6 billion francs in 1995. Sales rose to 162.1 billion francs in 1996 from 160.4 billion the year before.
It raised its net dividend to 10 francs per share, from eight francs in 1995, but the payout remained below the 14 francs it paid in the three years to 1994.
Debt fell significantly, with gearing dropping to 32 percent from 61 percent in 1995.

Investors liked what they heard and share-buying drove the share up by more than five percent to a high of 653 francs on Tuesday from a closing price of 613 francs on Monday, defying the downward trend in the overall blue-chip share index.
"The market is buying into the story that Alcatel is gradually being restructured...and is rewarding Serge Tchuruk," one share broker said.

Alcatel said it would pursue action to improve productivity this year, streamlining the organisation, optimising real estate holdings and reinforcing internal controls, notably via centralisation of the company's treasury.

"The actions already achieved or in progress, as well as our knowledge of developments in the group's main markets, underpin the objective of a return to a satisfactory level of profitability by 1998," it said.
